scam_types.name: Fake investment
scam_types.how_it_works: A stranger or a slick online ad promises high, steady returns, often in crypto or forex. A fake website shows 'profits' growing so the victim keeps adding money. Withdrawals are blocked unless more fees or taxes are paid.
red_flags: guaranteed or unusually high returns
pressure to invest quickly before an offer ends
found through social media, a messaging group or a 'mentor'
payment goes to a crypto exchange or a brand new account
asked to pay a fee or tax before withdrawing profits
pressure_tactics: small early payout to build trust
scam_types.safe_advice: Check the firm on the official regulator register. Real investments never guarantee returns. Never pay a fee to withdraw your own money.

scam_types.name: Fake bank or police call (safe account)
scam_types.how_it_works: A caller pretends to be from the bank's fraud team or the police and says the account is under attack. The victim is told to move money to a 'safe account' that the scammer controls.
red_flags: caller says your account is compromised and you must move money now
told not to tell anyone, including bank staff
payment is made while on a live phone call
caller asks you to ignore the bank's warning screens
new payee set up minutes before the payment
scam_types.safe_advice: A real bank never asks you to move money to keep it safe. Hang up and call the number on the back of your card.

scam_types.name: Romance scam
scam_types.how_it_works: A person met online builds a close relationship over weeks, then invents an emergency such as a hospital bill, a customs fee or a travel problem and asks for money.
red_flags: relationship is only online and they never meet or video call
sudden emergency that needs money
asks for gift cards, crypto or transfers to a third party
tells the victim to keep the relationship private
repeated requests that grow over time
scam_types.safe_advice: Never send money to someone you have not met in person. Talk to a friend or family member before paying.

scam_types.name: Tech support and remote access
scam_types.how_it_works: A pop-up or caller claims the computer is infected or a refund is due. The victim installs a remote-control tool, and the scammer then moves money from the victim's own banking session or tricks them into paying.
red_flags: a remote-control app is running during the banking session
caller asks the victim to install software
payment to an unrelated company for 'refund' or 'fix'
victim describes being guided step by step
screen is being shared
scam_types.safe_advice: Never let anyone control your device. Real support does not call you out of the blue.

scam_types.name: Invoice redirect (changed bank details)
scam_types.how_it_works: A scammer who has access to or copies a supplier's email sends a real-looking invoice with new bank details. A business or home buyer pays the wrong account.
red_flags: bank details changed by email shortly before payment
payee name does not match the supplier name
request marked urgent, with a deadline today
email address slightly different from the usual one
large one-off payment to a new account
scam_types.safe_advice: Phone the supplier on a number you already know to confirm new bank details before paying.

scam_types.name: Online purchase scam
scam_types.how_it_works: A seller on a marketplace advertises an item at a great price, asks for payment by bank transfer outside the platform, and then disappears.
red_flags: price far below the market
seller asks to pay outside the platform's protection
no way to see the item in person
new seller account with few reviews
pressure because 'others are interested'
scam_types.safe_advice: Use payment methods that protect buyers. If it looks too cheap, it probably is.

scam_types.name: Prize, inheritance or loan advance fee
scam_types.how_it_works: The victim is told they have won a prize, inherited money or qualified for a loan, but must first pay a fee, tax or insurance. The promised money never arrives.
red_flags: unexpected prize or windfall
a fee must be paid first
asked to pay quickly to an individual's account
official-looking but unverifiable documents
contact came by message, email or text
scam_types.safe_advice: Real prizes and loans do not ask for money upfront. Do not pay to receive money.

scam_types.name: Family emergency impersonation
scam_types.how_it_works: A message from an unknown number says 'Hi Mum, I lost my phone', then asks for an urgent transfer for a bill or an emergency.
red_flags: message from a new number claiming to be a relative
urgent request for money to a third party's account
relative cannot talk on the phone
asked to keep it secret from the rest of the family
payee name is not the relative
scam_types.safe_advice: Call the relative on the number you already have before sending anything.
